# <span id="aanchor376"></span> Meter Direction Editor

FLOWCAL ships with several pre-defined directions termed base directions, but the user can add their own custom directions via the Meter Direction Editor. These custom direction names allow for the creation of directions that conform to company standard naming conventions.

Custom Directions require a Base Direction of Inlet, Outlet, Throughput, Off System, or Both (In and Out). Directions are used by the location rollups process to determine the contribution of each location member. If enabled in FLOWCAL Options, location rollups subtotal location rollup values based on Meter Direction. These totals are then viewable by certain reports and in the Monthly and Daily Rollups, NGL Balance Viewer and the Recovery Analysis viewer.

Enable subtotaling by Meter Direction in the [FLOWCAL Configuration](FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md#Subtotal) screen.

<div class="procedure">

To view or edit meter directions:

1.  Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**.
2.  In the **Application** group, click **Meter Direction**.

<br/>![](data:image/png;base64,)

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Meter Direction Screen Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the Meter Direction screen:

1.  **Default Meter Directions** - Default directions are the basic meter directions that were used in FLOWCAL 7 that have been predefined in FLOWCAL. They cannot be modified or deleted.
2.  **User-Defined Meter Directions** - Examples of user-defined directions are Receipt with a base direction of Inlet and Delivery with a base direction of Outlet. Once meter directions are defined, a direction can be assigned to a meter by editing meter characteristics.
3.  **Reserved Directions** - Directions depicted in bold print have specific purposes and cannot be edited by a user.
4.  **Relationship** - The **Relationship** button is used to set a relationship between Meter Directions and Meter Classes, and is only visible when the Subtotal by Meter Direction and Meter Class options are enabled in the [FLOWCAL Configuration](FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md) screen. (This concept is covered in greater detail in the Meter Class section.)

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Creating">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Creating Meter Directions</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Creating">

<div class="procedure">

To create a new direction:

1.  Launch the Meter Direction Editor.
2.  Click **New**.
3.  Enter the direction details.
4.  Click **Save**.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Editing">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Editing Meter Directions</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Editing">

<div class="procedure">

To edit an existing direction:

1.  Launch the Meter Direction Editor.

2.  select an meter direction name from the list and click **Edit**.

    If a direction is assigned to one or more meters, the direction name is the only attribute that can be changed. Directions that have a bold font cannot be edited.

3.  To change or edit a meter direction name, click the **Name** field and enter a new direction name.

4.  Select a base direction from the drop-down menu. The base direction determines how meter and ticket data is used in gain/loss calculations, and how a meter or ticket is added to a location. Only directions that have a base direction of "Inlet" or "Outlet" can be assigned to a standalone ticket.

5.  Click **Save**.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Deleting">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Deleting Meter Directions</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Deleting">

<div class="procedure">

To delete a meter direction:

1.  Launch the Meter Direction Editor.
2.  Click on the meter direction to be deleted.
3.  Click **Delete**.

If a direction is assigned to one or more meters or tickets (i.e., it is still in use on at least one meter or ticket), it cannot be deleted.

</div>

</div>
